clue.text: Maybe Ian Paisley has the answer — get rid of South in uprising!

parts.note: the Reverend Ian Paisley, so an example of a clergyman, abbreviated Rev

indicators.note: tells you to throw the South out of the word for the answer

parts.note: an answer is a solution
S is the compass abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: A jibe that the Ulster firebrand's only solution is a Protestant rising with the South kept out.
explanation.walkthrough: Paisley was a minister, the Rev Ian Paisley. 'get rid of South' throws the S out of SOLUTION, leaving OLUTION; 'has' joins it to REV.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolution is a popular rising against those in power, so an uprising.

clue.text: Debased NUM role gets 'Yes' from former premier

indicators.note: something debased is corrupted and degraded, so these letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: Y is the short form of yes, as on a Y/N form

explanation.surface: A miners' union official compromised and won approval from an ex-Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: NUM is Britain's National Union of Mineworkers. 'Debased' rearranges NUM ROLE to MULRONE, and Y for yes follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Mulroney was Prime Minister of Canada from 1984 to 1993, so a premier of the recent past.

clue.text: Western with many twists grabs 'em while they're young

indicators.note: the word many is given twists, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A cowboy film full of plot turns about someone who snatches people in their youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twists' rearranges MANY to YMAN, joined by 'with' to W. Bill Wyman of the Rolling Stones began a relationship with Mandy Smith when she was thirteen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rolling Stones bassist was notorious for his affair with a schoolgirl, so the clue paints him as a snatcher of the young.

clue.text: Support for one who spouts "Prince despised state"

parts.note: odium is the state of being hated or despised

explanation.surface: A speechmaker's slogan attacking a royal and the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the wordplay look like a speech being made from the stand itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is a raised platform a speaker stands on to address an audience at length.

clue.text: Could be (if one replaced yob element) ideal Tory leader

indicators.note: the letters that follow could be arranged into something else, so they are reordered
one letter of the phrase is swapped out for another, the if merely setting up the condition

parts.note: an element of the word yob, its first letter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a perfect Conservative chief could emerge if loutish members were swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' swaps the Y of IDEAL TORY for I, giving IDEALTORI, and 'Could be' rearranges that. 'Leader' is the British name for a newspaper's main opinion piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader, or leading article, is a newspaper editorial giving the paper's own opinion.

clue.text: Maxwell (heaven finally acquired) to join House and mix with betters

indicators.note: the name has acquired a letter, which goes inside it

parts.note: the tycoon Robert Maxwell was nicknamed Cap'n Bob

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word heaven

parts.note: the word whose closing letter is taken

explanation.surface: The late press baron gets a place in the Lords and rubs shoulders with the grand.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Maxwell, the newspaper owner who died at sea in 1991, was known as Cap'n Bob. 'heaven finally' is its last letter, which 'acquired' puts inside to make BNOB; 'to join' puts the house in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to socialise familiarly, especially with people of higher rank.

clue.text: Severe criticism upset 1000 beastly lovers

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters bottom to top

parts.note: K stands for a thousand
the ALF, the Animal Liberation Front, a militant group of animal lovers

explanation.surface: Harsh words having stirred up a thousand animal-rights activists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns KALF to FLAK. The Animal Liberation Front was a British direct-action group of the 1980s and 90s.
explanation.definitionFit: Flak, from anti-aircraft fire, is used of a barrage of hostile criticism.

clue.text: Prescott tax holds record!

indicators.note: the tax word holds the record word inside it

parts.note: a duty is a tax on goods
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: John Prescott's tax plans include a record sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' makes the tax wrap round the record. John Prescott became Labour's deputy leader in 1994 and later Deputy Prime Minister, so the definition is a role rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Prescott was Labour's second-in-command, so he stands as an example of a number two.

clue.text: See 12
One on the lookout for dirt, note, seen around scruffy urinals

definitions.text: One on the lookout for dirt

indicators.note: the note is seen wrapped around the other letters

parts.note: a jot is a brief note

indicators.note: scruffy means untidy and messed up, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A muckraker caught lurking in grubby public lavatories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like part of a list but is a jot; 'scruffy' mixes the lavatory word into URNALIS, and 'seen around' wraps the jot round those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid reporter hunts for scandal, which the clue calls dirt.

clue.text: Blast recess, as they say in Lancashire!

indicators.note: in a Lancashire accent the word is pronounced with a long oo, like the bomb

parts.note: a nook is a small recess or corner

explanation.surface: A northern exclamation cursing a recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as they say in Lancashire' means the word for recess is spoken with a long northern oo. Lancashire is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To nuke is to blast with a nuclear weapon.

clue.text: Rich? Not America as presented by our double-barrelled compiler

parts.note: something rich is laughably absurd, as in that's rich
the Old World is Europe, Asia and Africa, as against the New World of the Americas

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter's wry aside about wealth and not being American.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher said it's a funny old world as she left office in 1990, and Private Eye took the phrase up.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase is offered as one the hyphenated setter might use himself, so this definition is loose.

clue.text: Feel a twinge, getting a pile of money from a hi-tech killer…

parts.note: to smart is to feel a sharp pain
a bomb is a large amount of money, as in costs a bomb

explanation.surface: A sharp pang on making a fortune from a high-tech weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bomb' is British slang for a lot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart bomb is a guided weapon steered onto its target by laser or satellite.

clue.text: This symbol of European union makes Mrs Titch to strangle abstainers

indicators.note: the letters hold the others tightly inside
Mrs Titch makes something new, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members abstain from drink

explanation.surface: Mocking the Prime Minister's wife throttling the teetotal over Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges MRS TITCH to MSTRICHT, which is set 'to strangle' AA, holding it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1992 treaty signed in this Dutch city created the European Union.

clue.text: Chief pain in the arse for Mandela?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Zulu leader's title was Chief

definitions.text: pain in the arse for Mandela?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Mandela's great rival, the start of his name sounding a little like butt and hell

explanation.walkthrough: Chief Mangosuthu Buthelezi led the Inkatha Freedom Party, whose feud with Mandela's ANC was bloody in the early 1990s; 'Chief' looks like an adjective but is his title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inkatha leader held the title Chief and was the great thorn in the ANC's side.

clue.text: … and is this the appropriate cost of one?

definitions.text: … and is this the appropriate cost of one?

parts.words: … and is this the appropriate cost of one?
parts.note: follows the previous clue: a smart weapon should cost a smart, that is tidy, amount

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 13 across: smart means tidy, so the fitting price for a smart bomb is a large sum of money with a tidy name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidy sum is a sizeable amount of money, which is what such weapons famously cost.

clue.text: Capital's hospital taking on old man! But there's an inital catch

indicators.note: the clue's spelling of initial: the catch comes at the start

parts.note: to bag something is to catch it
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
dad is an informal word for one's father, the old man

explanation.surface: A capital's hospital is taking on someone's father, but there's a snag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inital' is the clue's misspelling of initial: it sends the catch to the start. The capital's hospital in the surface is a false trail; the capital is the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Baghdad is the capital city of Iraq.

clue.text: Tory stalwart is a shower and phoney

parts.note: a hail is a shower of hailstones, or of anything
a sham is a fake or phoney

explanation.surface: A jibe that a loyal Conservative is a useless bunch and a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' is British slang for a useless lot, which colours the surface. Lord Hailsham was a Conservative Lord Chancellor for many years.
explanation.definitionFit: Quintin Hogg, Lord Hailsham, served Conservative governments for decades, a stalwart of the party.

clue.text: One half of Jeffrey (awful shit) is no supporter of the government

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
the first half of ARCHER, the surname of the Tory novelist Jeffrey Archer

indicators.note: awful suggests something mangled, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a disgraced Tory peer, calling him anti-government.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer was a Conservative politician and novelist. 'One half' looks like a single phrase, but One is AN and half of ARCHER is ARC; 'awful' rearranges SHIT to HIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An anarchist rejects all government, so is the opposite of a supporter of it.

clue.text: Eye again gets criticism

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to eye something is to view it

explanation.surface: Private Eye is once more on the receiving end of hostile comment.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital E nods to Private Eye, the satirical magazine this puzzle ran in.
explanation.definitionFit: A review is a critical assessment of a book, play or performance.

clue.text: Virginia's tizzies?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what Virginia is one of, a member of the American union
second meaning: tizzies are fits of agitation, as in getting into a tizzy

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests a woman's fits of nerves, but the two words define separately.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural word means both bouts of agitation and the political units of America.

clue.text: It's definitely pigs' excrement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for the police, also called pigs

explanation.walkthrough: 'It's definitely' is padding; pigs is not the farm animal but slang for police, who in Britain are also called the filth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a contemptuous term for the police and a name for foul dirt.

clue.text: Vacillating philanthropist occupying front half of celebrated US address

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the oil billionaire family whose trust funds museums

definitions.text: occupying front half of celebrated US address
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the first five of the ten letters of Lincoln's Gettysburg Address

explanation.walkthrough: The Getty fortune funds a major arts trust; Gettysburg Address, Lincoln's 1863 speech, begins with the same five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Getty family of oil billionaires endowed museums and galleries, so a giver of gifts to good causes.

clue.text: Sports car's back with shortened gear-changer — lousy transmission, though

indicators.note: the sports car is brought back, reading its letters from right to left

parts.note: MG is a British sports car maker
a transvestite changes gear, in the sense of clothes; TV is the short form

explanation.surface: A sports car's rear, a cut-down gearstick and a dodgy gearbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MG to GM. 'gear' means clothing, not a car part, so the changer is a transvestite, TV. GMTV was Britain's ITV breakfast service from 1993.
explanation.definitionFit: The breakfast channel's broadcasts are dismissed as poor viewing, a dig at a television service.

clue.text: House staff dropped by Ron

parts.note: the ceremonial staff of the House of Commons, which Labour MP Ron Brown seized and dropped in 1988

explanation.walkthrough: House staff suggests servants, but it is a ceremonial rod. Ron Brown grabbed it in the Commons chamber and let it fall during a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Commons' ornamental staff of office symbolises royal authority and must be present for the House to sit.

clue.text: He's involved with Persil ad — not what we've come to expect from our grey PM!

definitions.text: not what we've come to expect from our grey PM

indicators.note: the letters are tangled up together, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the HE of He's; its 's is just a link

explanation.surface: A man appearing in a washing-powder commercial is out of character for a drab Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' rearranges HE, PERSIL and AD. John Major was mocked as grey; Persil is a British washing powder.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm direction from the top was what critics said John Major's government lacked.

clue.text: Our old over-sexed Aussie would slip one into this former poll-watcher

definitions.text: Our old over-sexed Aussie would slip one into this
definitions.meaning: first meaning: Barry ..., Private Eye's lusty Australian strip cartoon hero, whose name slips one into the word
second meaning: Robert ..., the BBC's election-night analyst with the swingometer

explanation.walkthrough: Barry McKenzie was a 1960s-70s Private Eye cartoon character; Robert McKenzie analysed results on BBC election nights until 1979.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to a randy cartoon Australian and to a television pundit who interpreted election results.

clue.text: Pisspoor attempt to outflank anti-smokers

indicators.note: to outflank is to go round the sides, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a try is an attempt
ASH, Action on Smoking and Health, the UK anti-smoking campaign

explanation.surface: A feeble bid to get round the anti-smoking lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashy means worthless or of very low quality, as crudely put by pisspoor.
